claim: British Museum is free, open daily 10:00–17:00 with Friday late opening to 20:30; last entry 16:45 (Fridays 20:15).
British Museum's headline 2026 blockbuster is the Bayeux Tapestry loan from France, opening September 2026 (after a June visit), while the Hawaiʻi: A Kingdom Crossing Oceans show runs to 25 May 2026.
quote: The Bayeux Tapestry will go on display at the British Museum from September 2026 to July 2027. Hawaiʻi: a Kingdom Crossing Oceans runs until 25 May 2026.

claim: National Gallery's main paid 2026 exhibition open in June is Zurbarán (runs until 23 August 2026, admission from £20); the Sainsbury Wing reopened in 2025.
quote: Zurbarán runs until 23 August 2026. Admission from £20. A major work by Francisco de Zurbarán, one of the great painters of 17th-century Seville.

claim: Tate Modern opens a major Frida Kahlo retrospective on 11 June 2026 (runs to 3 May 2027) and an Ana Mendieta show on 25 June 2026, making it the highest-impact June 2026 blockbuster pick.
quote: Frida Kahlo, 11 June 2026 – 3 May 2027... Ana Mendieta, 25 June 2026 – 3 January 2027.

claim: Tate Modern is free to enter for the collection and stays open until 22:00 on Friday and Saturday — useful for evening visits.
quote: Tate Modern is open Friday and Saturday from 10am to 10pm. Entry to the collection is free.

claim: V&A South Kensington's June 2026 programme is anchored by Schiaparelli: Fashion Becomes Art (to 1 November 2026) and the new Design and Disability show opening 4 June 2026, with the permanent collection free.
quote: Schiaparelli: Fashion Becomes Art runs through 1 November 2026, the first major UK exhibition devoted to the innovative fashion house with over 200 objects. Design and Disability opens 4 June 2026.

claim: Natural History Museum (free) headline shows in June 2026 are Wildlife Photographer of the Year (to 12 July 2026) and the paid Jurassic Oceans: Monsters of the Deep (to 3 January 2027).
quote: Wildlife Photographer of the Year runs until July 12, 2026, the 61st edition. Jurassic Oceans: Monsters of the Deep runs until January 3, 2027.

claim: Science Museum (free) is running Future of Food (free ticketed, to 1 September 2026) and a Star Trek Warp Trail marking the franchise's 60th anniversary, alongside the Power Up video-game gallery.
quote: Future of Food, 24 July 2025 – 1 September 2026, is a free, ticketed exhibition for ages 7+. The Star Trek Warp Trail celebrates 60 years of Star Trek.

claim: The Wallace Collection (free permanent collection in a Manchester Square townhouse) is hosting Winston Churchill: The Painter (23 May–29 November 2026, paid) plus a free display The Wallace Collection at War (to 25 October 2026).
quote: Winston Churchill: The Painter, 23 May–29 November 2026, brings together more than fifty works. The Wallace Collection at War, free, 15 April–25 October 2026.

claim: Sir John Soane's Museum is free, walk-in, open Wednesday–Sunday 10:00–17:00 (last admission 16:30) at 13 Lincoln's Inn Fields — a small, idiosyncratic house-museum stuffed with Hogarths, Canalettos and the Sarcophagus of Seti I.
quote: Entry is free. The museum is normally open Wednesday to Sunday, 10am to 5pm, last admission 4:30pm. No need to pre-book.

claim: Courtauld Gallery (paid) at Somerset House opens Hepworth in Colour on 12 June 2026 (£18, to 6 September) plus free displays Studio Prints and Hepworth & Nicholson photographs — strong June 2026 picks for a focused 90-minute visit.
quote: Hepworth in Colour, 12 June – 6 September 2026, admission £18. Studio Prints: An Artists' Workshop, 6 June – 13 September 2026.

claim: Design Museum (Kensington, paid temporary exhibitions, free permanent gallery) headlines summer 2026 with Wes Anderson: The Archives and NIGO: From Japan with Love (to 4 October 2026), plus a free Mineral display opening in June.
quote: Wes Anderson: The Archives, the first retrospective devoted to his cinematic output. NIGO: From Japan with Love runs until 4 October. Mineral free display opens June 2026.

claim: Time Out's 2026 best-museums list keeps the British Museum, V&A, Tate Modern, National Gallery and Sir John Soane's at the top, and singles out the Design Museum and Imperial War Museum as strong supplementary picks.
quote: The Sir John Soane's Museum is the London home of architect Sir John Soane... resulting in this perfectly amazing place. The Design Museum completely devotes itself to contemporary design.

claim: Time Out names the new London Museum at Smithfield as the single best new thing to do in London in 2026, but the General Market galleries do not open until late 2026 — meaning it is unavailable for a June 2026 weekend visit.
quote: Time Out has named the London Museum as the best new thing to do in the capital in 2026, with its shiny new home in Smithfield Market.

claim: The former Museum of London (Barbican site) has been closed since December 2022 and rebrands as the London Museum opening at Smithfield 'towards the end of 2026' — so this major civic-history museum is unavailable during a June 2026 trip.
quote: The new London Museum opens towards the end of 2026 in the heart of the historic City of London, situated in breathtaking spaces and showcasing more of our collection than ever before.
